fact_notes: Dec 17, 1903, Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk: first flight 12 s, 120 ft, Orville at the controls; fourth flight (Wilbur, about noon) 59 s, 852 ft.
John T. Daniels of the Kill Devil Hills lifesaving station squeezed the shutter bulb; he had never taken a photograph.
Neither brother received a high-school diploma (Wilbur finished the course but the family moved before graduation; Orville left in his junior year).

Wilbur's letter to the Smithsonian is dated May 30, 1899 and contains 'I am an enthusiast, but not a crank in the sense that I have some pet theories as to the proper construction of a flying machine.'
Langley was Secretary of the Smithsonian; the War Department's Board of Ordnance and Fortification granted $50,000 (the Smithsonian added about $20,000).
Aerodrome A failed on launch from a houseboat on the Potomac on Oct 7 and Dec 8, 1903; Dec 8 to Dec 17 is nine days.
NYT editorial 'Flying Machines Which Do Not Fly', Oct 9, 1903: '...in from one million to ten million years.'
Wright expenses 1900-1903 including travel: a little under $1,000 (commonly cited, McCullough; Orville later said about $1,000).
Telegram text: 'Success four flights thursday morning ... longest 57 seconds inform Press home Christmas' (57 is the telegrapher's error for 59).
